summary: Duplicate corporate-card transaction lines from SpendOps feed causing reconciliation failure and blocking payment run
description:
Issue summary:
Corporate card transaction feed from vendor SpendOps is delivering duplicate line items for a subset of employee charges (same transaction_id with different item_id). The accounting reconciliation job flags these as potential zero-dollar refunds or duplicates, which prevents the weekly payment run from creating vendor/employee payouts.

Impact:
- Weekly payment run blocked for ~210 expense items (AP batch dated 2026-03-12).
- ~45 employees have reimbursements in Pending status; Finance cannot approve or release until duplicates are cleared.
- Temporary risk of missed reimbursements for payroll cutoffs.

Environment:
- Production corporate card ingestion pipeline (etl/card-ingest).
- SpendOps integration v2.3.1.
- Affected entities: Redwood US (default ledger), Redwood EU (small subset).

Steps to reproduce / observed behaviour:
1) SpendOps posts card feed to s3://redwood-spendops/ingest/2026-03-12/transactions.csv
2) ETL job card-ingest-prod-v3 picks up file and normalizes transactions into staging.card_txns table.
3) Normalize step groups lines by transaction_id; for ~210 transactions there are two distinct item_id values under the same transaction_id.
4) Reconciliation job (acct-recon-runner) marks those as duplicates and moves to manual_review queue, causing the payment-runner to abort AP batch creation.

Expected behaviour:
- Feed should contain one line per transaction_id; if vendor provides split-line items they should sum to the transaction amount and include a parent_id indicator. Reconciliation should accept proper split-lines and proceed.

Actual behaviour:
- Duplicate lines are near-identical: same transaction_id, same amount, different internal item_id; no parent_id or split-line metadata. The result is flagged as a potential duplicate instead of a legitimate split-line, halting automated payout creation.
steps_to_reproduce:
1. Download sample file attached from s3 path mentioned.
2. Run local normalization script used by etl (scripts/normalize_card_feed.py) against the file.
3. Observe duplicate rows with identical transaction_id but different item_id.
4. Re-run acct-recon-runner in dry-run mode to see items routed to manual_review.

comments: 2026-03-13 09:12 - Evelyn Martinez (Finance): Noticed that the weekly AP batch failed. Uploading a redacted sample CSV to the ticket and flagging for Payments/ETL. Priority due to payroll window.
2026-03-13 10:01 - Marcus Nguyen (Payments): Assigned. Initial triage shows ingestion marked duplicates. Reaching out to SpendOps for feed schema clarification. Adding eng/etl to ticket.

2026-03-13 13:45 - Priya Shah (ETL): Looked at normalize_card_feed.py and the staging rows. The feed lacks parent_id and split-amount metadata. Two hypotheses: 1) SpendOps introduced duplicate line emission bug; 2) Our dedupe logic misfires when merchant descriptors differ slightly.

2026-03-13 15:20 - Marcus Nguyen (Payments): Contacted SpendOps partner support (case #SP-28917). They acknowledged a recent deployment to split merchant-level detail that may have broken parent_id. They provided a corrective feed patch ETA 2026-03-14 18:00 UTC.

2026-03-14 08:55 - Finance Ops (Triage): We need a temporary workaround to unblock payments if SpendOps patch is delayed. Suggested option: safe-merge duplicates that have identical transaction_id and timestamp and same amount, limited to US entity and amounts < $500.

2026-03-14 11:30 - Marcus Nguyen (Payments): Eng/ETL prepared a safe-merge script and ran it against a test partition. Verified that merging clears manual_review for 184/210 items; remaining 26 require manual verification due to mismatched amounts or cross-currency flags.

2026-03-14 13:05 - Priya Shah (ETL): Note: applied safe-merge to staging-prod partition for date 2026-03-12 in a controlled run. AP batch generation proceeded. Finance confirmed payouts for 139 employees released in next payment window. Remaining items moved to manual reconciliation queue and owner assigned.

2026-03-14 16:40 - SpendOps Support: Patch v2.3.2 deployed. They added parent_id for split-lines and fixed duplicate emission for standard corporate card flows. Advised to validate 3 subsequent daily feeds.

2026-03-14 17:10 - Marcus Nguyen (Payments): Closing action items: follow up validation till 2026-03-17, update runbook, and create preventative monitoring. Leaving ticket open until final validation completed.
investigation_notes: Checked staging.card_txns: duplicate groups keyed on transaction_id 'tx_0b9c7d' appear 2x with identical amount and timestamp. No parent_id present.
Cross-checked SpendOps schema doc v2.3.1: parent_id is optional; v2.3.2 will make parent_id present for split lines. Partner confirms regression after their descriptor enhancement.

Safe-merge logic implemented: group by transaction_id, timestamp, and amount within 1 minute window; if count==2 and amount equal and currency same and amount < $500, merge into single logical item preserving both item_ids in metadata. Script id: etl/safe_merge_txns/merge-2026-03-14-11.
resolution: Temporary workaround applied: safe-merge script executed on staging partition for 2026-03-12. AP batch generation completed and partial payouts released. SpendOps deployed patch v2.3.2 to include parent_id for split-lines. Remaining follow-ups: monitor three days of incoming feeds for recurrence, add a reconciliation alert when duplicate groups > 5% of daily card volume, and update runbook to include safe-merge criteria and approvals. Finance to manually verify the 26 flagged items and confirm reimbursements.
